source.title: Few-Shot Self-Rationalization with Natural Language Prompts
source.authors: Ana Marasović; Iz Beltagy; Doug Downey; Matthew E. Peters

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates model-size scaling on few-shot self-rationalization task metrics, a downstream setting distinct from held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports a model-size sweep with accuracy and BERTScore results. These are downstream metrics, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy losses; it does not fit or test power laws for pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocations. Prompt comparisons in Sections 3 and 3.1–3.3 are not scaling results.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps model size (BASE 200M, LARGE 770M, 3B 2.8B) within one model family and reports downstream few-shot accuracy and explanation BERTScore on four FEB tasks plus CoS-E. This bears on V6 in a new downstream setting (few-shot self-rationalization). It has only three sizes and fits no curve, so it can show improvement with scale but not whether that improvement is predictable.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say accuracy, BERTScore and plausibility increase monotonically with model size on all datasets, and that the human-explanation gap remains large (GPT-3 is 25.7 points behind gold on average). However, their own label breakdown shows E-SNLI entailment plausibility does not scale with size. UnifiedQA-3B beats GPT-3 on accuracy and BERTScore except on SBIC, while GPT-3 explanations are more plausible.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes models on few-shot task examples or uses GPT-3 in-context demonstrations, and measures downstream accuracy and explanation quality rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset and evaluation setup: GPT-3 is below UNIFIED QA 3B on accuracy and BERTScore for E-SNLI, ECQA, and COMVE, but above it on SBIC. GPT-3 is evaluated using in-context demonstrations, while UNIFIED QA models are fine-tuned.
record.problems: The study measures downstream outcomes rather than pretraining loss and does not fit a quantitative scale curve or test extrapolation. GPT-3 is evaluated with a different method and a smaller dev set (18 rather than 350 examples); the authors did not perform GPT-3 prompt search. Reported standard errors reflect repeated random train-dev splits, whose sets may overlap.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 human plausibility values and label-specific plausibility breakdowns were not extracted; the table's flattened multi-label layout makes reliable assignment of some values difficult. Table 10 compares prompt choices rather than model-size scaling.

untested.parts: Predictability: no curve is fitted, no extrapolation is made, and only three sizes span about one order of magnitude. No test of downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.
No extrapolation from fitted small runs.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in other modalities or regimes.

missing.what: E-SNLI 'entailment' plausibility does not scale with size: 15.6, 27.3, 27.1 for BASE/LARGE/3B. Authors state it 'does not scale with the model size'. The rows_left_out declaration covers this, but a researcher would want it as a row bearing on V6.
missing.locator: Table 5, Label1 plausibility; Section 4.1 'Performance w.r.t. Labels'

missing.what: Overall human plausibility by size (e.g. ECQA 25.5→30.3→34.2; COMVE 13.8→25.6→33.4). Authors report a BASE-to-3B gain of 6.2-24.8, mean 14.8.

record.verdict_notes: Weak V6 evidence: there are three sizes, the downstream fine-tuning setup is few-shot, and GPT-3 is not comparable (different family, instruction-tuned, in-context evaluation, 18-example dev sets). The reader's GPT-3 'reversed'/'supports' labels are dropped as confounded. The reader's SBIC 'supports' label cited UnifiedQA rows r29-r30 instead of GPT-3 rows, which is incorrect. Standard errors come from 60 overlapping train-dev splits.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is not measured.
The study does not fit loss curves on small runs or test extrapolations to larger runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal split is tested.
Depth, width, and architecture variation at fixed parameter count are not tested.
The study does not test power-law forms for other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning loss, or transfer loss.
Tests downstream task accuracy and explanation BERTScore across model sizes in few-shot self-rationalization; it does not fit a predictive scale curve or test prediction from pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across setups.

relationships.condition: T5 (E-SNLI) and UnifiedQA (ECQA, COMVE, CoS-E) BASE→LARGE→3B, few-shot prompt fine-tuning with 48 examples
relationships.reason: Accuracy and BERTScore rise monotonically and substantially with size, e.g. ECQA accuracy 41.4→57.2→65.9 (r1-r6, r9-r14, r17-r22, r33-r38).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy and BERTScore increased monotonically and substantially with model size, including ECQA accuracy of 41.4→57.2→65.9.

relationships.reason: Gains nearly vanish from LARGE to 3B (accuracy 71.1→71.7, BERTScore 68.5→68.9, within about one standard error), so improvement with size is task-dependent (r25-r30).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rises only from 71.1 to 71.7 and BERTScore from 68.5 to 68.9, within about one standard error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: UNIFIED QA BASE, LARGE, and 3B on E-SNLI, ECQA, COMVE, SBIC, and C O S-E
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy and BERTScore increase monotonically across the three UNIFIED QA sizes for each dataset; see r1–r6, r9–r14, r17–r22, r25–r30, and r33–r38.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-3 compared with UNIFIED QA 3B on E-SNLI, ECQA, and COMVE
reader_labels.reason: Despite its larger stated size, GPT-3 has lower accuracy and BERTScore than UNIFIED QA 3B on these datasets; the study also uses a different in-context evaluation setup (r7–r8, r15–r16, r23–r24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: GPT-3's accuracy and BERTScore exceed the UNIFIED QA 3B values on SBIC (r29–r32).
